title: frictionBench operation
description: The Darcy friction factor's correlation library, in two parts. VERIFY (always): every registered correlation — Blasius, Colebrook-White, Haaland, Churchill — reproduces its own published anchor, and the deviation is printed beside the correlation's validity window and its primary citation. COMPARE (optional): all four are evaluated at the SAME Re and roughness, and the spread is published TWICE — over all of them, and over only those inside their stated windows. The two are reported apart because collapsing them would say 'the correlations disagree by 26 %' when the truth is 'three agree within 2 % and one was asked a question it was never fitted for'. The bench never says which correlation is right: that depends on the pipe, and ranking them would hide the choice the engineer has to make.

deviationTolerance.title: Anchor deviation tolerance
deviationTolerance.description: Allowed relative deviation of each correlation from its own published anchor; defaults to 0.03. Exists to honour the anchors' own rounding, never to let a failing correlation through — a coefficient that drifts should be fixed, not accommodated.

compare.title: Comparison point
compare.description: Optional. Evaluate every registered correlation at one hydraulic state and publish the spread. Omitting the block leaves only the verification half.

Re.title: Reynolds number
Re.description: The Reynolds number to compare at. Must be positive: a Reynolds number of zero is not a flow, and every correlation here divides by it.

relRough.title: Relative roughness eps/D
relRough.description: Wall roughness over diameter; defaults to 0 (hydraulically smooth). A non-zero value is what puts Blasius outside its window, since it carries no roughness term at all.

sweep.title: Reynolds-number sweep
sweep.description: Optional. Evaluate every registered correlation on one logarithmic grid of Re at each declared relative roughness and write one CSV row per (eps/D, Re): each correlation's f and its own window flag, the regime the engine names, and Churchill's two asymptotes fL = 64/Re and fT, whose 12-norm is Churchill's f. The correlations' own answers, never a new number.

file.title: CSV file name
file.description: The CSV the sweep writes, in the case directory. A path into data/standards/ is refused.

ReMin.title: Lowest Reynolds number
ReMin.description: The first grid point. Must be positive: the grid is logarithmic and every correlation divides by Re.

ReMax.title: Highest Reynolds number
ReMax.description: The grid runs to the last point at or below this value; must exceed ReMin.

pointsPerDecade.title: Points per decade
pointsPerDecade.description: Re_k = ReMin 10^(k / pointsPerDecade): a whole number, so a decade that starts on a grid point ends on one.

relRough.title: Relative roughnesses eps/D
relRough.description: One curve per value; at least one, each >= 0 (0 is the hydraulically smooth pipe).
